text: ya i mean the best example is likely the painter but doesnt matter, what do you need ? yes build it as a parts library, independent of the map project, not associated with it
resolution: Put the Studio into the V20 workspace branch/twig history as a PARTS LIBRARY independent of the map project (USER req_0993), modeled on the painter's cutout/stream.ts that the user pointed to. New editors/model/modelStream.ts is a per-concern stream (StoredPart carrying each part's serialized EditMesh + presentation; order-aware partAdded/MeshUpdated/Renamed/VisibilitySet/Reordered/Removed events; dumb-upsert materializer; unknown kinds pass through per V20). studioModel.ts was rewired from an in-memory store to a PROJECTION of that stream: it opens one route session (editorSessions().open('/studio', editorChannel(modelStream))) and every mutator commits a content event + labeled marker on the one cross-session chain, so parts now survive a reload AND each edit is a labeled undo point. The active part rides the twigs file (not the undo chain); undo/redo APPEND inverse events (V20 never-rewind) via a local inverse stack, wired to Ctrl+Z/Y (Ctrl+Shift+Z) plus a visible undo/redo control in StudioEditor. Falls back to a pure in-memory fold when the store is unavailable so the viewport never crashes. Tests: new modelStream.test.ts 4/4 (cold-reopen round-trip, order ops, unknown-kind passthrough, inverse cancels forward edit); editMesh 19/19 regression clean; Studio.tsx + full sources.ts chain bundle clean. Hot-reload TSX, nothing committed (user leads on commits). Follow-up: twig the viewport tool-state (selMode/gizmoTool/smooth/camera) and build the compose-into-map consumer.
